findings.title: enableSqlExpressions always returns false, leaving dead feature-flag logic and an unreachable SQL branch
findings.body: The new enableSqlExpressions function computes `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)` and then returns false on every path, so the feature-flag lookup is dead code and the entire `case QueryTypeSQL` body after the gate (lines 133-138) is unreachable. As written the code looks like a logic bug (an inverted check that is then discarded) and invites a future well-meaning 'fix' that flips it and silently re-enables the CVE-2024-9264 attack surface. If the intent is permanent removal, this should be an explicit `return false` (or an unconditional error at the call site) with a comment referencing the CVE; the accompanying user-facing message 'sqlExpressions is not implemented' is also misleading, since the feature is implemented but deliberately disabled for security reasons.

findings.title: No regression test for the CVE-2024-9264 fix
findings.body: This PR disables SQL expressions to fix a critical RCE/LFI vulnerability but adds or updates no tests. There is no test asserting that a SQL expression query (e.g. one using read_csv/read_blob against a local file, the known exploit shape) is rejected through the ExpressionQueryReader.ReadQuery path, and none asserting that NewSQLCommand/sql.TablesList now fail. A future change that re-implements pkg/expr/sql.DB or touches the inverted logic in enableSqlExpressions could silently re-open the vulnerability without any test failing. Additionally, any existing unit tests that exercised sql.TablesList or SQLCommand against the real DuckDB are not touched in this PR and would now fail against the always-erroring stub, so the test suite state for this package should be verified.

findings.title: Legacy SQL command path is blocked only implicitly via the stub DB error
findings.body: The reader.go gate explicitly rejects QueryTypeSQL, but the legacy parsing path (UnmarshalSQLCommand -> NewSQLCommand, used by the rawNode-based query parsing) has no explicit disable check. It is blocked only as a side effect of sql.TablesList now always returning 'not implemented' from the stub DB, which surfaces to users as the confusing 400 error 'error reading SQL command' instead of a clear 'SQL expressions are disabled' message. Functionally this does close the hole today (and the DuckDB dependency is removed from go.mod), but the protection relies on the stub never being re-implemented; if pkg/expr/sql.DB is ever given a real implementation, this path would re-enable SQL expression execution with no feature-flag or security gate. An explicit check or comment here would make the security invariant robust against future refactoring.
